title: Phishing
tagline: Spotting fake messages before they trick you.

scenes.narration: It was a quiet Saturday afternoon. Maya was finishing her homework on her tablet when her phone buzzed. A new message read: Congratulations! You have won a brand-new smartphone! Click this link within 10 minutes to claim your prize!

convo.text: Wow! I won a phone! I can't believe it!

scenes.narration: Just then, her friend Aarav walked into the room.

convo.text: What's so exciting?
Look! I won a new smartphone!
Did you enter a competition?
No, I don't remember entering one.
Do you know this person?
No. I've never seen this number before.

scenes.narration: Aarav pointed at the link and the message's urgent countdown.

convo.text: Look at the website address. It looks strange, and the message is trying to make you hurry.
Maybe they're trying to make me act without thinking.
Exactly. We should check before clicking.

scenes.narration: Maya searched for the company's official website. There was no information about any competition.

convo.text: This is phishing!
Yes. Phishing messages try to trick people into clicking harmful links or giving away personal information.
I'm glad I checked first.
Remember: stop, check, and think before you click.

title: Malware
tagline: Knowing what happens after a risky download.

scenes.narration: Aarav loved playing games on his computer. One afternoon he found a website offering a popular game for free, with a big button that read: DOWNLOAD FREE GAME.

convo.text: Awesome! I can get the game for free.

scenes.narration: A file appeared on his computer with a strange filename, then a pop-up flashed: Your computer is infected! Click here to fix it!

convo.text: Oh no! What's happening?
Where did you download that file from?
This website. It said the game was free.
Downloading files from unknown websites can be dangerous. The file could contain malware.
Malware? What's that?
Malware is harmful software that can damage your device or steal information.

scenes.narration: Maya helped Aarav close the suspicious pop-up. They deleted the downloaded file and ran a security scan.

convo.text: Next time, I'll only download software from trusted sources.
Good choice!

title: Password Security
tagline: Building passwords that are hard to guess.

scenes.narration: Maya wanted to create an account for a new learning website. It asked her to create a password, so she quickly typed: maya123.

convo.text: Done! That's easy to remember.

scenes.narration: Aarav saw the password over her shoulder.

convo.text: Maya, that password is very easy to guess.
But it's my name and a number. What's wrong with that?
Someone who knows you might easily guess it.

scenes.narration: Aarav explained that a strong password should be long, difficult to guess, and not based on easily known personal information.

convo.text: So I shouldn't just use my name or birthday?
Right. And don't reuse the same password everywhere.
Now I understand!

title: Privacy & Online Safety
tagline: Thinking twice before sharing personal details.

scenes.narration: Sita was excited about her new school. She took a picture outside her house, opened her social media app, and started writing a post about being home alone, with exactly where she lived and how close her school was.
Maya saw the post before Sita hit share.

convo.text: Wait, Sita. Do you really want everyone to know where you live?
Hmm, I didn't think about that.
Some information is better kept private.

scenes.narration: Maya pointed out exactly what was risky in the post.

convo.text: Your home location and school details are personal information. Sharing them publicly can put your privacy at risk.
I'll think carefully before sharing personal information online.
